questions.question: Give the advantages and disadvantages of road transport.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages: flexibility and door-to-door delivery, speed over short and medium distances, departure whenever the load is ready, access to rural areas and farms without railways, and lower building cost per kilometre than railways. Disadvantages: small load per vehicle, so many trucks and more fuel per tonne for bulk goods; damage to road surfaces; congestion; more air pollution and greenhouse gases per tonne than rail; and serious accidents. Road suits small loads, short and medium distances and places without railways.

questions.question: Give the advantages and disadvantages of rail transport.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages: very large capacity for bulk goods such as coal, iron ore, grain and containers; less fuel and pollution per tonne over long distances; fewer trucks on the roads, so less congestion, road damage and accidents; electric trains; and cheap mass commuter transport. Disadvantages: trains go only where there are tracks, so trucks are usually needed at the ends; railways are very expensive to build and need gentle gradients; timetables and loading make rail slow for small urgent loads; and in South Africa under-investment, locomotive shortages, poor maintenance, cable theft and vandalism have made services unreliable.

questions.question: What are the requirements for future transport networks in South Africa?
questions.expected_answer: Future networks need maintenance and reliable services; a better balance with more bulk and long-distance freight on rail; integration of roads, railways, ports, airports and pipelines through intermodal terminals; safety and security against theft and vandalism; sustainability through less pollution, cleaner vehicles and good public transport; access for rural and township communities; and regional links with faster border crossings. For example, one 3 000-tonne train can replace about 89 trucks of 34 tonnes.
